messages.subject: Path Modeling
parts:
Dear Lavaan  groups,

I want to apply Path Model for my data on fertility determinants and and watched the lavan youtube files. However, I have one question if you can help me. I want to model a panel data on a path model. My data is panel observation for the dependent and explanatory variables. But theoretically some of the variables are proximate determinants whereas others are distant variables that affect the proximate determinants. I guess using a simple multi level panel data analysis will result in biased estimates. Hence I want to see the direct effects of the proximate determinants and the indirect effects of the distal factors.

Is there any possibility that I can use panel data with in Path Model.

example
model <- '
fertility~FP+Marriage+Lactation+Sterility (all observations are panel, no latent variable)
mariage~ethnic+gdp+region+education+infantmr
lactation~ethnic+gdp+region+education+infantmr
FP~ethnic+gdp+region+education+infantmr
Sterility~ethnic+gdp+region+education+infantmr

'
I understand that individual models in lavaan example use simple OLS regression (or correlation), and my question is how can I make the individual models with in the path model to be panel models


Regards
--
Gizachew Balew
Doctoral Student
Graduate School of Public Health, Health Demography
Seoul National University, South Korea

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Path Modeling
parts:
I don't see what would stop you from running this model.  Does the syntax not work?  (make sure the variable names are consistent: Marriage vs. mariage).  

A "Panel model" is fit to longitudinal data.  I don't see anything in your syntax that indicates you have measured the same variables repeatedly, but if that is what you have, you can just regress the first-occasion outcomes on your distal predictors, then regression second-occasion outcomes on the first-occasion outcomes, third-occasion outcomes on second-occasion outcomes, and so on.  That is typically the kind of model that I see, but you can run whatever model you want (e.g., if you are interested in predictions for the last occasion, you might want to regress the last occasion on the distal outcomes instead of or in addition to regressing the first occasion on the distal outcomes).

This isn't really a lavaan issue so much as figuring out what model you want to fit to your data.  You might get more feedback about fitting models to panel data on a more general forum like SEMNET.

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Terry
